```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Models and source

Yao 2025 describes how population PK modelling selected the patient dose of
simnotrelvir, an oral SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease inhibitor marketed co-packaged
with ritonavir 100 mg as a pharmacokinetic booster. The paper fits two
independent NONMEM models, and both are in the library:

* **Model 1** (`Yao_2025_simnotrelvir_healthy`): fitted to the first-in-human
  phase Ia trial in healthy adults, with and without ritonavir. The authors
  used it to choose the 750/100 mg twice-daily (BID) patient dose
  (Supplementary Table S3).
* **Model 2** (`Yao_2025_simnotrelvir`): the final model, refitted to the
  ritonavir-boosted data of phase Ia plus the phase Ib and phase II/III
  patient trials (Supplementary Tables S4-S6).

```{r load-models}
ui1 <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yao_2025_simnotrelvir_healthy"))
ui2 <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yao_2025_simnotrelvir"))
```

* Citation: `r ui2$reference`
* Model 1: `r ui1$description`
* Model 2: `r ui2$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00614-25> (open access; Model 2 and
  both dose simulations are in the supplementary information)

Both models are two-compartment with first-order absorption after a lag,
exponential between-subject variability on CL, Vc and Ka, inter-occasion
variability on Vc between the first-dose and steady-state sampling occasions,
and combined proportional and additive residual error. Ka falls with the
simnotrelvir dose (a power function of the dose in mg), and food raises both
Ka and the relative bioavailability F. Ritonavir enters differently:

* Model 1 multiplies CL by 0.241 with ritonavir, uses a separate dose exponent
  on Ka, and raises F relative to monotherapy by 1.36 when ritonavir is given
  with the simnotrelvir dose or by 1.61 when it was given 12 h before.
* Model 2 has only boosted data, so CL carries no ritonavir term and instead
  rises with creatinine clearance; F is 1.15-fold higher when ritonavir was
  given 12 h before the dose than when it is given with it.

# Population

```{r population}
str(ui1$population)
str(ui2$population)
```

Model 1 used 1742 concentrations from 72 healthy Chinese adults in the phase
Ia trial (NCT05339646): median age 30 years (20-50), median weight 64.4 kg
(46.1-82.9), 26.4% female, median creatinine clearance 117 mL/min (Table 1).
24 subjects took simnotrelvir alone (150-3000 mg single dose or 750-1500 mg
BID) and 60 took it with ritonavir 100 mg (250-1200 mg single dose, 150-750 mg
BID, and a 750 mg fasted/fed food-effect part); 12 of them contributed to
both. Model 2 dropped the monotherapy data and added 24 phase Ib and 98 phase
II/III patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19, for 182 subjects and 1634
concentrations: median age 35 years (18-67), median weight 65.0 kg (39.0-115),
35.7% female, median creatinine clearance 113 mL/min (64.8-230). Only 12
subjects (in the food-effect part) were dosed fed.

# Source trace

| Model element | Model 1 value (Table 2) | Model 2 value (Table S5) |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2 compartments, first-order absorption with lag | Results; eResults | eResults |
| `lcl` (CL, L/h) | 174 (monotherapy) | 22.6 at CRCL 113 mL/min |
| `e_conmed_rtv_cl` (Ritonavir-CL) | 0.241 | -- |
| `e_crcl_cl` (CRCL-CL) | -- | 0.39, as `(CRCL/113)^0.39` (footnote a) |
| `lvc` (V2, L) | 33.7 | 9.48 |
| `lvp` (V3, L) | 3.84 | 3.92 |
| `lq` (Q, L/h) | 58.6 | 17.4 |
| `lka` (Ka, 1/h) | 0.425 | 0.755 |
| `e_dose_ka*` (DOSE-Ka) | -0.127 alone, -0.138 with ritonavir (footnotes c-e) | -0.229 (footnote b) |
| `e_fed_ka` (FOOD-Ka) | 1.49 | 1.51 |
| `lfdepot` (F1) | 1, fixed | 1, fixed |
| `e_fed_fdepot` (FOOD-F1) | 1.39 | 1.36 |
| `e_conmed_rtv_fdepot` (Ritonavir-F1, with the dose) | 1.36 (footnote g) | -- |
| `e_conmed_rtv_pre12h_fdepot` (Ritonavir-F1, 12 h before) | 1.61 (footnote h) | 1.15 |
| `ltlag` (ALAG, h) | 0.223 | 0.447 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalka` (IIV, CV%) | 27.1, 83.0, 19.4 | 27.0, 81.6, 16.0 |
| `etaiov_vc_1`, `etaiov_vc_2` (IOV on V2, CV%) | 69.1 | 117.5 |
| `propSd` (proportional) | 46.0% | 35.9% |
| `addSd` (additive, ng/mL) | 1.556 | 1.463 |
| Concentration scaling | `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` (mg/L to ng/mL) | same |

Variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`, the exact relation for the exponential IIV
model the supplement's Equation (1) describes.

# Coding the ritonavir-timing covariate

`CONMED_RTV_PRE12H` is set per dose record: 1 when a ritonavir dose was given
12 h before this simnotrelvir dose, 0 when ritonavir is given with it. With
both drugs given twice daily from the same first dose, only the first
simnotrelvir dose has no ritonavir on board from 12 h earlier, so the first
dose carries 0 and every later dose carries 1. `OCC` is 1 over the first
dosing interval and 2 over the steady-state interval.

rxode2 evaluates `f(depot)` with the covariate values in force at the dose
time. When an observation and a dose share a time (here the 12 h trough and
the second dose), both records must carry the same covariate value, or the
dose can pick up the observation's value. The helper below therefore codes
the covariates by time, not by record type.

```{r event-helper}
dose_times <- seq(0, 108, by = 12) # 10 doses; the last is the steady-state interval
obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(108, 120, by = 0.25))))

make_events <- function(subjects, per_dose_timing) {
  dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id, time = obs_grid) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    left_join(subjects, by = "id") |>
    mutate(
      amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, dose, 0),
      DOSE = dose,
      FED = 0L,
      CONMED_RTV = 1L,
      CONMED_RTV_PRE12H = if (per_dose_timing) as.integer(time >= 12) else 0L,
      OCC = ifelse(time <= 12, 1L, 2L)
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, DOSE, FED, CONMED_RTV, CONMED_RTV_PRE12H, OCC, CRCL)
}
```

A typical-value check that the flag reaches the dose: with every random effect
at zero, the bioavailability of the second dose is 1.15 in Model 2 and the
first dose's is 1.

```{r flag-check}
chk_ev <- make_events(tibble(id = 1L, dose = 750, CRCL = 113), per_dose_timing = TRUE)
chk <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui2), chk_ev, returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = TRUE)
f_by_dose <- chk |> filter(evid == 1L) |> pull(fdepot)
f_by_dose
stopifnot(f_by_dose[1] == 1, all(abs(f_by_dose[-1] - 1.15) < 1e-12))
```

# Closed-form check of clearance, bioavailability and units

For a single dose the AUC to infinity must equal `1000 * F * dose / CL` in
ng*h/mL. The table checks this for the typical subject in each model under
the covariate combinations that change F or CL, with PKNCA computing the AUC
from the simulated profiles.

```{r closed-form}
sd_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.05), seq(4.25, 48, by = 0.25))))
scen <- tribble(
  ~scen, ~model, ~label,                                ~CONMED_RTV, ~CONMED_RTV_PRE12H, ~FED, ~CRCL, ~cl,                 ~f,
  1L,    1L,     "Model 1: alone, fasted",              0L,          0L,                 0L,   113,   174,                 1,
  2L,    1L,     "Model 1: ritonavir with dose",        1L,          0L,                 0L,   113,   174 * 0.241,         1.36,
  3L,    1L,     "Model 1: ritonavir 12 h before",      1L,          1L,                 0L,   113,   174 * 0.241,         1.61,
  4L,    1L,     "Model 1: ritonavir with dose, fed",   1L,          0L,                 1L,   113,   174 * 0.241,         1.36 * 1.39,
  5L,    2L,     "Model 2: with dose, CRCL 113",        1L,          0L,                 0L,   113,   22.6,                1,
  6L,    2L,     "Model 2: 12 h before, CRCL 113",      1L,          1L,                 0L,   113,   22.6,                1.15,
  7L,    2L,     "Model 2: with dose, CRCL 70, fed",    1L,          0L,                 1L,   70,    22.6 * (70 / 113)^0.39, 1.36
)
sd_ev <- tidyr::expand_grid(scen = scen$scen, time = sd_grid) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central") |>
  bind_rows(tibble(scen = scen$scen, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 750, cmt = "depot")) |>
  left_join(scen, by = "scen") |>
  mutate(id = scen, DOSE = 750, OCC = 1L) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
ev_cols <- c("id", "time", "evid", "amt", "cmt", "DOSE", "FED", "CONMED_RTV", "CONMED_RTV_PRE12H", "OCC", "CRCL")

sd_sim <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui1), sd_ev |> filter(model == 1L) |> select(all_of(ev_cols)),
                  returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui2), sd_ev |> filter(model == 2L) |> select(all_of(ev_cols)),
                  returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE)
) |>
  left_join(select(scen, id = scen, label), by = "id")

sd_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(filter(sd_sim, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | label + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(sd_ev |> filter(evid == 1L) |> select(label, id, time, amt), amt ~ time | label + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
auc_cmp <- as.data.frame(sd_nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(select(scen, label, cl, f), by = "label") |>
  mutate(auc_closed = 1000 * f * 750 / cl, pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / auc_closed - 1))
auc_cmp |>
  select(label, PPORRES, auc_closed, pct_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Scenario = label,
    `AUCinf, PKNCA (ng*h/mL)` = PPORRES,
    `1000 * F * dose / CL` = auc_closed,
    `% diff` = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
# Both sides use the same parameters: only trapezoid and extrapolation error remain.
stopifnot(nrow(auc_cmp) == 7, all(abs(auc_cmp$pct_diff) < 2))
```

# Model 1: replicating the dose selection (Supplementary Table S3)

The authors simulated 300, 450, 600 and 750 mg simnotrelvir with ritonavir
100 mg BID in the fasted state and reported the first-dose and steady-state
trough concentration (Ctrough) and AUC0-12, and the share of subjects whose
steady-state Ctrough exceeded the protein-binding-corrected Omicron EC90 of
274 ng/mL. Each arm here has 200 subjects with between-subject and
inter-occasion variability; the 12 h concentration is the trough. The 108-120
h interval (the 10th dose) is steady state, which this model reaches within a
day.

The authors' table is reproduced when `CONMED_RTV_PRE12H` is 0 on every dose,
i.e. with the "ritonavir given with the dose" bioavailability factor (1.36)
throughout. That arm is compared with Table S3 below; a 750 mg arm with the
per-dose coding (first dose 0, later doses 1) is simulated alongside it to
show what the 1.61 factor would do at steady state.

```{r m1-sim}
n_per_arm <- 200
arms1 <- tibble(
  arm = 1:5,
  Regimen = c("300/100 mg BID", "450/100 mg BID", "600/100 mg BID", "750/100 mg BID",
              "750/100 mg BID, per-dose timing"),
  dose = c(300, 450, 600, 750, 750),
  per_dose = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
subj1 <- tibble(arm = rep(arms1$arm, each = n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), CRCL = 117) |>
  left_join(arms1, by = "arm")

ev1 <- bind_rows(
  make_events(subj1 |> filter(!per_dose) |> select(id, dose, CRCL), per_dose_timing = FALSE),
  make_events(subj1 |> filter(per_dose) |> select(id, dose, CRCL), per_dose_timing = TRUE)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251101)
sim1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui1, ev1, returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE) |>
  left_join(select(subj1, id, Regimen), by = "id")
```

```{r nca-helper}
run_interval_nca <- function(sim, ev, subj) {
  conc <- bind_rows(
    sim |> filter(time <= 12) |> mutate(Interval = "First dose", tint = time),
    sim |> filter(time >= 108) |> mutate(Interval = "Steady state", tint = time - 108)
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(Regimen, Interval, id, tint, Cc)
  dose <- ev |>
    filter(evid == 1L, time %in% c(0, 108)) |>
    left_join(select(subj, id, Regimen), by = "id") |>
    mutate(Interval = ifelse(time == 0, "First dose", "Steady state"), tint = 0) |>
    select(Regimen, Interval, id, tint, amt)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ tint | Regimen + Interval + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ tint | Regimen + Interval + id),
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, auclast = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE)
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "clast.obs"))
}
nca1 <- run_interval_nca(sim1, ev1, subj1)
```

`clast.obs` is the concentration at the end of the 0-12 h interval, i.e. the
trough before the next dose.

```{r m1-compare}
ref_s3 <- tribble(
  ~Regimen,          ~Interval,      ~clast.obs, ~auclast,
  "300/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   240,        8098,
  "300/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 284,        9587,
  "450/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   379,        11934,
  "450/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 449,        14129,
  "600/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   525,        15697,
  "600/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 622,        18583,
  "750/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   672,        19394,
  "750/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 795,        22959
)
s3_tab <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca1 |> filter(Regimen %in% ref_s3$Regimen),
  reference = ref_s3,
  by = c("Regimen", "Interval"),
  units = c(clast.obs = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(s3_tab, digits = 0,
             caption = "Medians: Yao 2025 Supplementary Table S3 vs simulation (Model 1, ritonavir-with-dose factor on every dose).")
cat(attr(s3_tab, "footnote"))
```

```{r m1-gate}
s3_pct <- nca1 |>
  group_by(Regimen, Interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(
    ref_s3 |> pivot_longer(c(clast.obs, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("Regimen", "Interval", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(s3_pct) == 16)
c(median_pct = median(s3_pct$pct), q90_abs_pct = unname(quantile(abs(s3_pct$pct), 0.9)))
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed CL, F or ritonavir factor moves every row by
  # tens of percent.
  abs(median(s3_pct$pct)) < 8,
  # Envelope over the 16 cells, robust to which subjects land in the tails.
  quantile(abs(s3_pct$pct), 0.9) < 15
)
```

The per-dose coding leaves the first dose unchanged but gives the steady-state
doses the 1.61 factor, so steady-state exposure is about 1.61 / 1.36 = 1.18
times higher, and further above Table S3:

```{r m1-perdose}
nca1 |>
  filter(grepl("^750", Regimen)) |>
  group_by(Regimen, Interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Ctrough (ng/mL)` = clast.obs, `AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)` = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "750/100 mg BID medians under the two codings of the ritonavir-timing flag (Model 1).")
```

The medians above are taken from the individual predictions (`Cc`). The
spread of the published troughs, and with it the share of subjects above the
EC90, is reproduced only when residual error is added, i.e. from the
simulated observations (`sim`), so the authors' trough percentiles and target
attainment were evidently computed from simulated observations. Without
residual error the 10th-90th percentile range of the 750 mg trough is about
410-1140 ng/mL instead of the published 239-1389 ng/mL, and nearly every
subject clears the EC90.

```{r trough-helper}
trough_summary <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    filter(time %in% c(12, 120)) |>
    mutate(Interval = ifelse(time == 12, "First dose", "Steady state")) |>
    group_by(Regimen, Interval) |>
    summarise(
      p10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), p50 = median(sim), p90 = quantile(sim, 0.9),
      pta = 100 * mean(sim > 274),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r m1-pta}
ref_s3_trough <- tribble(
  ~Regimen,          ~Interval,      ~ref_p10, ~ref_p50, ~ref_p90, ~ref_pta,
  "300/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   83,       240,      526,      42.2,
  "300/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 98,       284,      622,      52.3,
  "450/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   133,      379,      810,      68.3,
  "450/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 158,      449,      959,      75.4,
  "600/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   185,      525,      1099,     81,
  "600/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 220,      622,      1302,     85.6,
  "750/100 mg BID",  "First dose",   239,      672,      1389,     87.2,
  "750/100 mg BID",  "Steady state", 283,      795,      1645,     90.6
)
tr1 <- trough_summary(sim1) |>
  inner_join(ref_s3_trough, by = c("Regimen", "Interval"))
tr1 |>
  transmute(
    Regimen, Interval,
    `Table S3 median (P10-P90)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", ref_p50, ref_p10, ref_p90),
    `Simulated median (P10-P90)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", p50, p10, p90),
    `Table S3 % > EC90` = ref_pta,
    `Simulated % > EC90` = pta
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Trough concentrations with residual error (ng/mL) and target attainment: Yao 2025 Supplementary Table S3 vs simulation (Model 1).")
```

```{r m1-figure, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
band <- function(sim) {
  bind_rows(
    sim |> filter(time <= 12) |> mutate(Interval = "First dose", tint = time),
    sim |> filter(time >= 108) |> mutate(Interval = "Steady state", tint = time - 108)
  ) |>
    group_by(Regimen, Interval, tint) |>
    summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.1), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(lo > 0) # log axis: drop the pre-lag zeros
}
ggplot(band(sim1 |> filter(!grepl("per-dose", Regimen))), aes(tint, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 274, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
  facet_grid(Interval ~ Regimen) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Simnotrelvir (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figure S3 of Yao 2025: median and 10th-90th percentile; dashed line is the EC90 274 ng/mL.")
```

# Model 2: replicating the 750/100 mg simulation (Supplementary Table S6)

Model 2 is simulated for 750/100 mg BID fasted with the per-dose coding (first
dose 0, later doses 1). The paper does not say which creatinine clearance its
simulation used; the cohort median of 113 mL/min, the model's reference
value, is used for every subject.

```{r m2-sim}
coding2 <- tibble(
  arm = 1:3,
  Regimen = c("Per-dose timing", "With dose on every dose", "12 h before on every dose")
)
subj2 <- tibble(arm = rep(coding2$arm, each = n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), dose = 750, CRCL = 113) |>
  left_join(coding2, by = "arm")
ev2 <- bind_rows(
  make_events(subj2 |> filter(arm == 1L) |> select(id, dose, CRCL), per_dose_timing = TRUE),
  make_events(subj2 |> filter(arm == 2L) |> select(id, dose, CRCL), per_dose_timing = FALSE),
  make_events(subj2 |> filter(arm == 3L) |> select(id, dose, CRCL), per_dose_timing = FALSE) |>
    mutate(CONMED_RTV_PRE12H = 1L)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251102)
sim2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui2, ev2, returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE) |>
  left_join(select(subj2, id, Regimen), by = "id")
nca2 <- run_interval_nca(sim2, ev2, subj2)
```

```{r m2-compare}
ref_s6 <- tribble(
  ~Regimen,          ~Interval,      ~clast.obs, ~auclast,
  "Per-dose timing", "First dose",   924,        26362,
  "Per-dose timing", "Steady state", 1249,       37758
)
s6_tab <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca2 |> filter(Regimen == "Per-dose timing"),
  reference = ref_s6,
  by = c("Regimen", "Interval"),
  units = c(clast.obs = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(s6_tab, digits = 0,
             caption = "Medians: Yao 2025 Supplementary Table S6 (750/100 mg BID) vs simulation (Model 2).")
cat(attr(s6_tab, "footnote"))
```

```{r m2-gate}
s6_pct <- nca2 |>
  filter(Regimen == "Per-dose timing") |>
  group_by(Regimen, Interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(
    ref_s6 |> pivot_longer(c(clast.obs, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("Regimen", "Interval", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(s6_pct) == 4)
s6_pct$pct
# With 200 subjects and IOV of 117% CV on Vc the Monte Carlo error of a
# median trough is several percent; a wrong F, CL or CRCL term moves these
# by 15% or more (see the codings compared below).
stopifnot(abs(median(s6_pct$pct)) < 8, max(abs(s6_pct$pct)) < 15)
```

Coding the flag the same on every dose cannot reproduce both columns of
Table S6: with 0 throughout the steady-state exposure is too low, and with 1
throughout the first-dose exposure is too high, each by about the 15% that
the factor 1.15 carries.

```{r m2-codings}
nca2 |>
  group_by(Regimen, Interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename(Coding = Regimen, `Ctrough (ng/mL)` = clast.obs, `AUC0-12 (ng*h/mL)` = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Model 2 medians under three codings of the ritonavir-timing flag; Table S6 gives 924 / 1249 ng/mL and 26362 / 37758 ng*h/mL.")
```

As for Model 1, the published trough spread and target attainment match the
simulated observations (with residual error):

```{r m2-pta}
ref_s6_trough <- tribble(
  ~Regimen,          ~Interval,      ~ref_p10, ~ref_p50, ~ref_p90, ~ref_pta,
  "Per-dose timing", "First dose",   424,      924,      1780,     96.5,
  "Per-dose timing", "Steady state", 556,      1249,     2497,     97.9
)
tr2 <- trough_summary(sim2) |>
  inner_join(ref_s6_trough, by = c("Regimen", "Interval"))
tr2 |>
  transmute(
    Interval,
    `Table S6 median (P10-P90)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", ref_p50, ref_p10, ref_p90),
    `Simulated median (P10-P90)` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", p50, p10, p90),
    `Table S6 % > EC90` = ref_pta,
    `Simulated % > EC90` = pta
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Trough concentrations with residual error (ng/mL) and target attainment: Yao 2025 Supplementary Table S6 vs simulation (Model 2).")
```

```{r trough-gate}
tr_all <- bind_rows(tr1, tr2)
tr_pct <- tr_all |>
  transmute(
    p10 = 100 * (p10 / ref_p10 - 1),
    p50 = 100 * (p50 / ref_p50 - 1),
    p90 = 100 * (p90 / ref_p90 - 1)
  ) |>
  unlist()
c(
  median_abs_pct_percentiles = median(abs(tr_pct)),
  median_abs_pta_points = median(abs(tr_all$pta - tr_all$ref_pta))
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(tr_all) == 10,
  # Read off the individual predictions instead (no residual error), the
  # 750 mg P10 is 40-70% too high and its target attainment about 10 points
  # too high; with 200 subjects per arm the Monte Carlo error of a single
  # 10th percentile is about 10-20%.
  median(abs(tr_pct)) < 15,
  median(abs(tr_all$pta - tr_all$ref_pta)) < 5
)
```

```{r m2-figure, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(band(sim2 |> filter(Regimen == "Per-dose timing")), aes(tint, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 274, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~Interval) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Simnotrelvir (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates Supplementary Figure S10 of Yao 2025: 750/100 mg BID, median and 10th-90th percentile.")
```

Supplementary Table S7 reports the Bayesian (post hoc) exposures of the 95
phase II/III patients rather than a simulation, so it is not a check of the
typical-subject model: a median predicted AUC of 45310 ng*h/mL and a median
observed Ctrough of 1522 ng/mL, both higher than the Table S6 simulation the
authors made with the same model.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Meaning of the ritonavir-timing flag.** Neither model's report says how
  "ritonavir 12 h before" was coded in the dataset. It is defined here per
  dose record (1 when a ritonavir dose was given 12 h before this simnotrelvir
  dose). For Model 2 this coding (first dose 0, later doses 1) is the only one
  of the three tried that reproduces both the first-dose and the steady-state
  columns of Table S6. The authors' Model 1 dose-selection simulation (Table
  S3) is instead reproduced with 0 on every dose, i.e. with the 1.36
  "ritonavir with the first simnotrelvir dose" factor at steady state as well;
  the per-dose coding puts the steady-state exposures about 18% higher than
  Table S3. Both are shown above.
* **Direction of the creatinine clearance effect.** The supplementary eResults
  say "the clearance of simnotrelvir decreased with increased creatinine
  clearance", but the printed equation `CL = 22.6 * (CRCL/113)^0.39` (Table S5
  footnote a), the positive estimate with a bootstrap interval of 0.213-0.568,
  and the Discussion ("a positive correlation was observed between
  simnotrelvir clearance and creatinine clearance") all give CL increasing with
  CRCL. The model follows the equation.
* **Creatinine clearance in the simulations.** The covariate values used in the
  authors' simulations are not reported. Model 2 is simulated at the cohort
  median, 113 mL/min, for every subject; Model 1 has no CRCL term (its CRCL
  effect was removed at backward elimination, Table S2).
* **Number of subjects in Model 1.** The main text says 60 volunteers, while
  Table 1 and the supplementary eResults give 72; 60 is the number who took
  ritonavir. The model metadata uses 72.
* **Occasions.** Both models estimate inter-occasion variability on V2 between
  the first and second intensive sampling occasions (supplementary eResults),
  with one variance shared by both occasions. `OCC = 1` is the first-dose
  occasion and `OCC = 2` the steady-state occasion; `OCC = 0` switches the
  occasion term off. The simulations above include it.
* **Residual error in the published simulations.** The supplement does not
  say whether its simulated concentrations include residual error. The
  medians do not depend on it, but the published trough percentiles and
  target attainment of both models are reproduced only with it, so the
  trough distributions are compared on the simulated observations (`sim`)
  and the AUC and median comparisons on the individual predictions (`Cc`).
* **Cohort size.** The authors repeated their Monte Carlo simulation 100 times;
  each arm here has 200 subjects, so the medians carry a few percent of Monte
  Carlo error.
